In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best technique for accelerometer-based activity recognition depends on the application, the type of activity and the data set.
no single technique is best suited for all activities.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the string-based methods provide the most accurate results, but are the least efficient in terms of computational time.
we present a survey of the state-of-the-art techniques for accelerometer data processing and compare the results from the different techniques.

we have shown that the best performing method for accelerometer-based activity recognition is to use a string-based approach that uses an n-gram model with the highest n value (n=5) and the longest sliding window (1 second) with an overlap of 50% between the windows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the string-based techniques are able to extract the activity information more efficiently and accurately than the other techniques.
the most accurate technique is a combination of a classical signal processing technique (the FFT) with a string matching algorithm.
, although some methods perform better than others for specific activities, none of the tested methods is able to provide an accurate representation of the activity for all activities.
